req.title: Return 404 on unknown post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-022 requires HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or POST /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id. Tests must cover: (1) positive — valid post id returns 200 for update; (2) negative — non-existent post id returns 404 for both update and delete; (3) boundary — id just above the highest existing post (21) returns 404, and id 0 (below minimum) returns 404. We also test both HTTP methods (GET and POST) for update, and POST for delete. Login is required, so we authenticate as a valid user whose posts exist in the pre-loaded data. Post 2 belongs to user Rahul (id=1), so we log in as Rahul to access update/delete on post 2. Non-existent ids tested: 9999 (far out of range), 21 (boundary: one above max existing id 20), and 0 (boundary: below minimum valid id).

tests.name: test_update_existing_post_returns_200
preconditions: Database contains pre-loaded 20 posts and 5 users
Post id=2 exists and belongs to user Rahul (id=1)
User Rahul is logged in
expected: Response body contains post title 'Pillow delta willow'
trace: R-FLASKR-022: valid post id must NOT return 404
EP: valid id partition returns 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_existing_post_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Pillow delta willow' in r.data

test_update_existing_post_returns_200()
